{{Short description|Azerbaijani mathematician (1936–2023)}}
'''Tamilla Nasirova''' ({{langx|az|Tamilla Nəsirova}}; 20 October 1936 – 12 April 2023) was an Azerbaijani mathematician. She specialized in [[probability theory]] and is known for her discoveries pertaining to the [[semi-Markov process]]. She was a professor at [[Baku State University]] from 1980 to 2018 and at the [[Karadeniz Technical University]] from 1996 to 2000. Nasirova was the first woman to earn a doctorate in mathematics in Azerbaijan and the first [[Azerbaijan|Azerbaijani]] woman to become a professor of mathematics.

== Biography ==
Tamilla Nasirova was born in [[Nəvahı]], Azerbaijan on 20 October 1936.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Azerbaijan's first female mathematician D.Sc and Prof. passed away |url=https://apa.az/en/social/azerbaijans-first-female-mathematician-dsc-and-prof-passed-away-400695 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230414013852/https://apa.az/en/social/azerbaijans-first-female-mathematician-dsc-and-prof-passed-away-400695 |archive-date=2023-04-14 |access-date=2023-04-14 |website=Apa.az |language=en}}</ref> She attended School No. 176 in [[Baku]] and graduated in 1953. She enrolled in [[Azerbaijan State University]] (now Baku State University) and graduated in 1958. After studying at the [[Ukrainian Academy of Sciences]] and [[Moscow State University]], she earned a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] at the [[Tashkent University of Information Technologies]] in 1964.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-04-12 |title=Tamilla Nəsirova vəfat etdi |trans-title=Tamilla Nasirova has died |url=http://pravda.az/news/110647 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230414013903/http://pravda.az/news/110647 |archive-date=2023-04-14 |access-date=2023-04-14 |website=Pravda.az |language=az}}</ref> In 1980, Nasirova was given a position as an associate professor of mathematics at Baku State University,<ref name=":0" /> becoming the first woman to hold such a position in Azerbaijan.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2016-10-20 |title=Azərbaycanın ilk qadın riyaziyyatçı professoru Tamilla Nəsirovanın 80 illik yubileyi qeyd olundu |trans-title=The 80th birthday of Azerbaijan's first female mathematics professor Tamilla Nasirova was celebrated |url=https://isi.az/az/news/80 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211022164703/https://isi.az/az/news/80 |archive-date=2021-10-22 |access-date=2023-04-14 |website=isi.az |language=az}}</ref> She became a full professor in 1995. She also taught at the [[Karadeniz Technical University]] in Turkey from 1996 to 2000.<ref name=":0" /> Nasirova continued teaching at Baku State University until 2018,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Nasirova Tamilla Khilal – Institute of Control Systems |url=https://isi.az/index.php?mod=content&id=92&lang=en |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230414013942/https://isi.az/index.php?mod=content&id=92&lang=en |archive-date=2023-04-14 |access-date=2023-04-14 |website=isi.az}}</ref> teaching [[probability theory]] and [[mathematical statistics]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Zeynalova |first=Vafa |date=2017-02-15 |title=Making the Science |url=http://regionplus.az/en/articles/view/6147 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201124203802/http://regionplus.az/en/articles/view/6147 |archive-date=2020-11-24 |access-date=2023-04-14 |website=Region Plus}}</ref>

Nasirova worked in probability theory and is known for her work involving [[semi-Markov process]]es,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> proving the ergodic theorem of semi-Markov processes and advancing several related developments that influenced their study.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /> Nasirova was a researcher for the [[Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences]] Institute of Control Systems for much of her life, beginning in 1958, continuing until 1980, and resuming her work in 1994.<ref name=":0" /> During her career, she published a total of 96 scientific works and trained ten doctoral students.<ref name=":2" /> She was awarded three Azerbaijani Certificates of Honor: two from Baku State University in 2007 and 2016, and one from the National Academy of Sciences in 2016. She was also recognized as an Honored Teacher of the Republic in 2009.<ref name=":2" /> Nasirova died on 12 April 2023, at the age of 86.<ref name=":0" />
